## Key question 1: Papers that compute dimensions by bracket depth of the Lie algebra generated by Hamiltonian functions

### Takeaway
Yes, this exists for the two-generator case T (kinetic) and V (potential): McLachlan–Ryland (2003) and
McLachlan–Murua (2019) define and compute the "Lie algebra of classical mechanics", graded by degree, and its
growth rate ("entropy" about 1.8249). No paper was found that generates from the *pairwise sub-Hamiltonians*
H_ij = T_i + T_j + V_ij of an N-body problem, or from any family of non-homogeneous (T+V-type) generators.

### Cited Findings
- McLachlan & Ryland, "The algebraic entropy of classical mechanics", J. Math. Phys. 44 (2003) 3071–3087
  (arXiv math-ph/0210030, DOI 10.1063/1.1576904). Introduces a "polynomially graded" class of Lie algebras,
  gives an algorithm for the dimensions c_n of homogeneous subspaces of the Lie algebra generated by kinetic
  and potential energy, and computes the entropy lim c_n^{1/n} ≈ 1.82542377420108 —
  [arXiv abstract](https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0210030); [AIP](https://aip.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.1576904)
- The same paper states that {V,{V,{V,T}}} vanishes identically, so the algebra is never free, "regardless
  of T, V, or the dimension of the system" — [search snippet of arXiv math-ph/0210030](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math-ph/0210030)
- McLachlan & Murua, "The Lie algebra of classical mechanics", J. Comput. Dyn. 6(2) (2019) 345–360
  (arXiv 1905.07554, DOI 10.3934/jcd.2019017; special issue in honour of R. Quispel). Abstract: because the
  kinetic energy is quadratic in momenta, the Lie algebra generated by T and V "obeys identities beyond those
  implied by skew symmetry and the Jacobi identity"; the universal object is called the Lie algebra of
  classical mechanics; it is "a direct sum of an abelian part and a part freely generated by the kinetic
  energy" (the abelian part "spanned by modified potential energies"); the growth rate (entropy) of the
  homogeneous dimensions is about 1.8249; the paper conjectures that the class of systems with Euclidean
  kinetic-energy metrics is already free (no further identities). It also states that the McLachlan–Ryland
  construction "is in error starting at order 13" — [AIMS](https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/jcd.2019017);
  [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.07554); [Semantic Scholar](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/e4b6809dff9ccb215438692806c4f4d6de363957)
- Grading used: "the Lie algebra of classical mechanics is the free Lie algebra [in the polynomially graded
  class] where A has degree 2 and B has degree 0" (A = kinetic, B = potential) — [arXiv 1905.07554 snippet](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.07554)
- McLachlan–Murua also count "the order conditions at each order n as the dimension of the degree-n part of
  that algebra" and link this to "free RKN trees" of earlier work; the algebra is "usually infinite
  dimensional" — [arXiv 1905.07554 snippet](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.07554)
- A 2026 quantum-chemistry Trotter review states that McLachlan and Murua showed the Lie algebra generated by
  the Laplacian and a multiplicative potential under the commutator is isomorphic to the Lie algebra of
  classical mechanics — [arXiv 2606.30741](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.30741)
- The same McLachlan–Ryland line also computed dimensions for *cubic potentials* and found them "remarkably
  small for small n" — [search snippet, arXiv math-ph/0210030 / 1905.07554](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.07554)
- Three-generator case in integrator literature: Laskar & Vaillant, "Dedicated symplectic integrators for
  rotation motions", Celest. Mech. Dyn. Astron. 131:15 (2019), arXiv 1809.04546. Splits the free-rigid-body
  Hamiltonian into three parts; remainders lie in "the Lie algebra generated by a three-element alphabet,
  associated with the Poisson brackets", graded by length of Lie monomials; "the number of independent
  equations at order k is given by the dimension of the Lie algebra L_k" —
  [HAL](https://hal.sorbonne-universite.fr/hal-02089463); [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.04546v2)
- Munthe-Kaas & Owren, "Computations in a free Lie algebra", Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 357 (1999) 957–981:
  generalises Witt's formula to arbitrary gradings (the counting tool used in all of the above) —
  [typeset.io copy](https://typeset.io/pdf/computations-in-a-free-lie-algebra-34cy1go7dw.pdf)
- Related LMS J. Comput. Math. paper gives explicit dimension formulae for graded subspaces of "free
  hierarchical algebras" arising in geometric integration —
  [Cambridge](https://resolve.cambridge.org/core/journals/lms-journal-of-computation-and-mathematics/article/on-the-dimension-of-certain-graded-lie-algebras-arising-in-geometric-integration-of-differential-equations/DC61335B0E7A178C21EF7E768926A2EE)
- Terminology check: the phrase "dynamical algebra" for the Poisson-closed set of functions appears in a
  fibre-bundle formulation of classical mechanics ("the subset of C^1 functions closed under addition, scalar
  multiplication and Poisson brackets ... a special kind of Lie algebra") — [arXiv physics/0109033](https://arxiv.org/pdf/physics/0109033);
  no paper using "dynamical Lie algebra" to mean the bracket-generated filtration of a finite set of classical
  Hamiltonians with dimension counts was found.
- Three-body "hidden algebra" / closure literature (Turbiner, solv-int/9805003; Iachello "Algebraic theory of
  the three-body problem" 1995) concerns finite-dimensional hidden symmetry algebras of quantum/integrable
  systems, not bracket-generation by pairwise Hamiltonians — [arXiv solv-int/9805003](https://arxiv.org/abs/solv-int/9805003)

### Inferences
- The McLachlan–Ryland/McLachlan–Murua object is graded by polynomial degree in p (A degree 2, B degree 0),
  which for a single T and V also coincides with a bracket-length-type grading. The N-body pairwise generators
  H_ij = T_ij + V_ij are *inhomogeneous* in this grading, so their algebra is not literally covered by those
  papers; it is however a Lie subalgebra of the algebra generated by {T_1..T_N, V_12, ...}, which is the
  multi-generator analogue of the classical-mechanics algebra. This connection is an inference; no source
  makes it.
- The "RKN Lie algebra" of the integrator literature is exactly the McLachlan–Murua object; the standard name
  in the literature is "Lie algebra of classical mechanics" (2019) or "polynomially graded Lie algebra" (2003).

### Gaps
- The actual table of dimensions c_n (by degree/length) from either McLachlan paper could not be retrieved
  (arXiv and ar5iv blocked). The caller should open arXiv 1905.07554 (Table 1 / Theorem 1) directly.
- Whether the algebra equals Free(T,V)/⟨[V,[V,[V,T]]]⟩ exactly, or has further relations, is not settled by
  the snippets. The 2019 structure theorem ("abelian part spanned by modified potentials ⊕ part freely
  generated by T") and the statement that the 2003 construction errs "starting at order 13" indicate the
  structure is subtler than a single-relation quotient, but no snippet states the ideal of relations.
- No citing paper from 2020–2026 computing dimensions for several generators (N-body) was found.

## Key question 2: Is "free modulo [V,[V,[V,T]]]" a known result, and what are the per-length dimensions (RKN counts)?

### Takeaway
The vanishing of {V,{V,{V,T}}} for T quadratic in p is standard and is the basis of the reduced RKN
order-condition counts in Blanes–Casas–Murua (2008, Table 2), Blanes–Casas–Escorihuela-Tomàs (2022, Table 1,
column ℓ_r) and the Acta Numerica review (2024, Table 2.1, column d_n). The numeric columns themselves were
not visible in any snippet and are reported here as a gap.

### Cited Findings
- Blanes, Casas & Murua, "Splitting and composition methods in the numerical integration of differential
  equations", Bol. Soc. Esp. Mat. Apl. 45 (2008), arXiv 0812.0377: has a Table 2 comparing the number of
  independent order conditions for splitting methods in the RKN case versus the general case; "up to order
  three the order conditions are the same in both cases" —
  [ehu.eus PDF](https://www.ehu.eus/ccwmuura/research/BSema08.pdf); [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.0377)
- Blanes, Casas & Murua, "Splitting methods for differential equations", Acta Numerica (2024), arXiv
  2401.01722: order conditions are independent when the elementary operators F_1, F_2, F_12, F_122, F_112, ...
  form a basis of the free Lie algebra on {1,2} (Lyndon basis); for RKN-type problems "the differential
  operators F_1 and F_2 satisfy a nested commutator identity identically, so the order conditions for
  multi-indices with some index at least 4 need not be considered"; Table 2.1 lists counts c_n (general) and
  d_n (RKN) for orders up to 11 — [Cambridge](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/acta-numerica/article/splitting-methods-for-differential-equations/2C1BD434F8D2052E593A755351B3ACA3);
  [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.01722)
- Blanes, Casas & Escorihuela-Tomàs, "Runge–Kutta–Nyström symplectic splitting methods of order 8", Appl.
  Numer. Math. 182 (2022) 14–27: Table 1 lists s_r (symmetric compositions), n_r (general splitting), ℓ_r
  (RKN) — "the RKN case is where many terms vanish identically, so their conditions can be ignored" —
  [ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0168927422001842);
  [UJI repository PDF](https://repositori.uji.es/server/api/core/bitstreams/be9da140-c382-4a1f-888f-7be546c4d208/content)
- Hairer–Lubich–Wanner, Geometric Numerical Integration, Chapter III "Order Conditions, Trees and B-Series":
  the chapter "terminates with the Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff formula, which allows another access to the order
  properties of composition and splitting methods" — [Springer chapter](https://rd.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007%2F3-540-30666-8_3.pdf).
  No snippet showed the RKN/[[B,A],B],B discussion; the book's RKN order-condition treatment (Sect. III.3/IV)
  must be checked directly.
- Calvo & Sanz-Serna (BIT 1992), "Order conditions for canonical Runge–Kutta–Nyström methods": canonicity
  conditions act as simplifying assumptions that lower the number of independent order conditions —
  [UVa report](https://hermite.uva.es/maripaz/reports/C-SS_1992.pdf)

### Inferences
- Since F_1 (kinetic) and F_2 (potential) satisfy [F_2,[F_2,[F_2,F_1]]] = 0 identically, the RKN count d_n is the
  dimension of the degree-n part of Free(A,B)/I where I contains ad_B^3 A. Whether d_n equals exactly the
  single-relation quotient dimension is NOT confirmed by any source found; McLachlan–Murua (2019) is the
  paper that answers this and should be read.

### Gaps
- The numeric sequences d_n / ℓ_r (RKN order-condition counts) were not visible in any snippet; I did not
  reconstruct them from memory. Sources: Table 2 of arXiv 0812.0377, Table 1 of the 2022 paper, Table 2.1 of
  arXiv 2401.01722.
- No source was found that calls this object "the RKN Lie algebra" by name; the names in use are "Lie algebra
  of classical mechanics" (McLachlan–Murua) and "RKN case / RKN-type splitting" (Blanes–Casas–Murua).

## Key question 3: Dullin 2013, "The Lie–Poisson structure of the reduced n-body problem"

### Takeaway
Dullin reduces the n-body problem by the Galilean group using polynomial (quadratic) invariants; the
reduced phase space carries a Lie–Poisson structure isomorphic to sp(2n−2) for any spatial dimension d, and
a kinetic/potential splitting yields a Poisson integrator. It is a kinematic closure result on quadratic
invariants, not an iterated-bracket filtration, and contains no dimension-by-bracket-length counts in any
retrieved description.

### Cited Findings
- Bibliographic: H. R. Dullin, Nonlinearity 26(6) (2013) 1565–1579, arXiv 1207.5883 —
  [OSTI record](https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/22296098); [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.5883);
  [MaRDI](https://portal.mardi4nfdi.de/wiki/Publication:2839484)
- Abstract: reduction by the Galilean symmetry group via polynomial invariants gives a Lie–Poisson structure
  isomorphic to sp(2n−2) "regardless of the spatial dimension d"; the reduced Hamiltonian retains the form
  kinetic (velocities only) + potential (positions only); "the splitting allows us to construct a Poisson
  integrator for the reduced n-body problem which is efficient away from collisions for n = 3"; the figure
  eight orbit "could be integrated in 18 time steps" — [arXiv 1207.5883](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1207.5883);
  [UTB catalogue record](https://vufind-test.katalog.k.utb.cz/SummonRecord/FETCH-LOGICAL-c322t-5ec124eb5e4069493461593b3eff593848a01ccc86635f3474af0be758921e4f3)
- Mechanism: "using quadratic invariants gives the sp(2n−2) structure, as was shown using different bases of
  invariants in [12] and [1]" — [arXiv 1207.5883 snippet](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1207.5883)
- The splitting is into kinetic and potential parts, each with an explicit Poisson-map flow; symmetric
  (Strang) composition gives second order — [arXiv 1207.5883, Sect. 6 snippet](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1207.5883)
- Discrepancy in secondary sources: Dullin's 2012 Fields Institute slides say "Figure 8 in 18 steps"; a 2011
  Groningen colloquium abstract says the figure-8 is computed "in 3 steps" —
  [Fields slides](https://gfsha1.fields.utoronto.ca/programs/scientific/12-13/Marsden/presentations/Dullin.pdf);
  [RUG abstract](https://www.rug.nl/news/2011/12/collow06122011)
- Follow-ups: Arunasalam, Dullin & Nguyen, "The Lie-Poisson structure of the symmetry reduced regularised
  n-body problem", arXiv 1408.2957 (regularised reduced 3-body problem has Lie–Poisson structure of type
  u(3,3)); Dullin & Montgomery, "The n-body problem on coadjoint orbits", arXiv 2504.01272 (Poisson
  structure inherited from sp(2n−2)*) — [arXiv 1408.2957](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1408.2957);
  [arXiv 2504.01272](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.01272)
- The repository's own earlier literature pass (docs/related_literature_2026-07-19.md) records the same
  reading: Lemma 1 (symplectic bracket on quadratic forms closes to sp(2m)) and Theorem 4 (Galilean reduction
  gives sp(2n−2)), with the caveat that "his sp(4) is a kinematic algebra of quadratic invariants (any
  potential), not an iterated-bracket filtration" — local file, consistent with the snippets above.

### Inferences
- Dullin's sp(2n−2) is the bracket-closure of the *quadratic* polynomial invariants (an honest
  finite-dimensional Lie algebra), which is why it coincides with the harmonic-potential closure (dim 15 for
  n = 3, sp(4) ≅ so(3,2), dim 10, plus translations/affine part — the repo's note attributes dim 15 to the
  affine extension). The paper does not compute, and is not about, growth of an iterated-bracket filtration
  generated by non-quadratic (1/r etc.) pair potentials.

### Gaps
- Full text not accessible; whether any explicit Lie algebra "generated by the splitting terms" is discussed
  (beyond the standard splitting) could not be verified. The 3-step vs 18-step figure-eight claim conflict
  is unresolved from snippets.

## Key question 4: Growth / Gelfand–Kirillov dimension of finitely generated Lie subalgebras of polynomial Poisson algebras

### Takeaway
No published theorem of the exact form "a finitely generated Lie subalgebra of the polynomial Poisson algebra
on R^{2n} has GK dimension ≤ 2n" was found. Adjacent verified results: Bavula's bound GKdim ≤ n for isotropic
(Poisson-commutative) subalgebras of P_{2n}; GKdim(A_n) = 2n for the Weyl algebra; Petrogradsky's results that
Lie algebras of vector fields have intermediate growth while free f.g. Lie algebras have exponential growth;
Riley–Usefi's bound GKdim ≤ cn for virtually-nilpotent f.g. Lie algebras.

### Cited Findings
- Definition: for a f.g. algebra A with generating subspace V, GKdim A = limsup log dim(V^1+...+V^r)/log r;
  polynomial growth iff finite GK dimension — [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gelfand%E2%80%93Kirillov_dimension)
- Bavula, "Gelfand–Kirillov dimension of commutative subalgebras of simple infinite dimensional algebras and
  their quotient division algebras" (arXiv math/0401263): "the Gelfand–Kirillov dimension of every isotropic
  subalgebra of the polynomial Poisson algebra P_{2n} is ≤ n"; the Weyl algebra A_n is central simple of
  GK dimension 2n — [arXiv math/0401263](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0401263)
- Riley & Usefi, "Lie algebras with finite Gelfand–Kirillov dimension", Proc. AMS 133 (2005) 1569–1572: a
  f.g. Lie algebra with a nilpotent ideal of class c and finite codimension n has GKdim ≤ cn; f.g. virtually
  nilpotent Lie algebras have polynomial growth — [AMS](https://www.ams.org/journals/proc/2005-133-06/S0002-9939-05-07618-5)
- Petrogradsky: "free finitely generated Lie algebras have exponential growth, while Lie algebras of vector
  fields have ... intermediate growth"; hierarchy of growth functions with level q = 1 finite-dimensional, q = 2
  polynomial growth — [USP seminar abstract](https://www.ime.usp.br/~liejor/2013/seminars_2013/liejor_2013/Abstract/petrogradsky_16_05_13.html);
  Petrogradsky, "On some types of intermediate growth in Lie algebras", Russian Math. Surveys (1993) —
  [mathnet.ru](https://mathnet.ru/eng/rm1339)
- Petrogradsky showed there exist Lie algebras of any GK dimension ≥ 1 (cited in Bartholdi's branch-group
  survey) — [arXiv math/0101222](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0101222)
- Petrogradsky–Shestakov self-iterating Lie algebras (char p, generated by derivations of truncated polynomial
  rings) have polynomial growth with GKdim = ln p / ln((1+√5)/2) — [J. Lie Theory 19 (2009)](https://www.heldermann.de/JLT/JLT19/JLT194/jlt19038.htm)
- Monotonicity: GK dimension of a subalgebra does not exceed that of the ambient algebra (stated for conformal
  algebras; standard in general) — [arXiv math/0005258](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0005258)
- The Lie algebra po(2n) of polynomials in (q,p) under Poisson bracket is a nontrivial central extension of
  the Hamiltonian Lie algebra h(2n), and polynomial growth is discussed for Z-graded Lie algebras —
  [arXiv math/0510019](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0510019)
- Open-problem statement: which conditions on a Poisson bracket make the associated Lie algebra finitely
  generated or finitely presented; H(2n) and K(2n+1) are simple and finitely presented —
  [Univ. Oviedo offprint](https://digibuo.uniovi.es/dspace/bitstream/10651/51059/1/1.off-print.pdf)
- Krause & Lenagan, Growth of Algebras and Gelfand–Kirillov Dimension, rev. ed., AMS GSM 22 (2000): standard
  reference (contents: growth of algebras; GK dimension of algebras and related algebras; localization;
  enveloping algebras) — [Edinburgh preprint page](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~tom/preprints.html);
  [catalogue](https://theses.univ-nantes.fr/vufind/Record/PPN052348296/TOC)

### Inferences
- Elementary bound (inference, no source): if the generators are polynomials of degree ≤ k on R^{2m}, a Lie
  monomial of length ℓ has polynomial degree ≤ ℓ(k−2)+2 because {f,g} lowers total degree by 2. Hence the
  span of all Lie monomials of length ≤ ℓ lies in the polynomials of degree ≤ ℓ(k−2)+2, whose dimension is
  O(ℓ^{2m}); so the Lie subalgebra has GKdim ≤ 2m = GKdim of the polynomial ring (Krause–Lenagan standard
  example). For k = 2 (quadratic generators) the degree stays ≤ 2 and the algebra is finite-dimensional
  (this is the Dullin/sp case). For *non-polynomial* generators such as 1/|q_i−q_j| the argument needs a
  weight filtration (e.g., by order of pole and degree in p) and the bound is not automatic; no source
  handles this.
- The RKN/classical-mechanics algebra has exponential growth (entropy ≈ 1.8249 < 2^... ; strictly less than the
  free two-generator rate), which is consistent with infinite GK dimension; this contrasts with the
  polynomial bound above because T and V are treated as *abstract* generators there (universal algebra),
  not as fixed polynomials on a fixed R^{2m}.

### Gaps
- No theorem specifically about GK dimension (or polynomial growth) of finitely generated Lie subalgebras of
  Poisson algebras of polynomial/rational functions was found under any query tried. Suggested follow-up
  (not performed): zbMATH/MathSciNet search for "Poisson algebra" + "Gelfand-Kirillov" + "Lie subalgebra";
  Petrogradsky's publication list for growth of subalgebras of W_n / H_n.

## Key question 5: Appearances of 3, 6, 17, 116 (A395423) and 3, 3, 8, 17, 44, 103, 272, 572 outside OEIS

### Takeaway
The only web hit for 3, 6, 17, 116 in this context is the user's own GitHub repository
(bshepp/3body-poisson-algebra). The per-length sequence 3, 3, 8, 17, 44, 103, 272, 572 returned no match
anywhere. The comparison sequence 3, 3, 8, 18, 48, 116, 312, 810 is confirmed as Witt's formula for the free
Lie algebra on 3 generators (OEIS A027376). oeis.org itself was unreachable from this environment.

### Cited Findings
- GitHub repository bshepp/3body-poisson-algebra: "Headline N=3 sequence 3, 6, 17, 116 is universal across
  potentials (1/r, 1/r², log, Yukawa, …), spatial dimensions, mass ratios"; dim(L1) = N(3N−5)/2 checked for
  N = 3..26; N = 9 gives L0 = 36, L1 = 99, L2 = 1107; a neural-network variant gives [3, 6, 17, 119] —
  [GitHub](https://github.com/bshepp/3body-poisson-algebra). (This is the same project as the present
  working directory; it is not an independent appearance.)
- Search for the exact string "3, 3, 8, 17, 44, 103, 272, 572": no matching page; nearest hits were
  unrelated OEIS entries (A105163, A180380, A026679, …) and a puzzle page for 5, 8, 17, 44 —
  [OEIS A105163](https://oeis.org/A105163/list)
- Search for "OEIS A395423": returned only neighbouring entries A395422 and A395424, not A395423 itself —
  [A395424](https://oeis.org/A395424/list); [A395422](https://oeis.org/A395422/list)
- Witt's formula dim L_n(3) = (1/n) Σ_{d|n} μ(d) 3^{n/d} gives 3, 3, 8, 18, 48, 116, 312, 810 for n = 1..8
  (hand-checked in the search result for n = 2, 3, 4, 8) — [Witt formula background](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1302.4123)
- The repo's earlier literature pass (local docs/related_literature_2026-07-19.md) explains the search
  invisibility: the public oeis.org/A395423 page was an allocation stub while the draft sat under
  oeis.org/draft/, which robots.txt disallows; it also records that OEIS search for 3, 6, 17, 116 returned
  zero results and that no third-party mention existed as of 2026-07-19.

### Inferences
- The per-length numbers 3, 3, 8 (lengths 1–3) coincide with the free algebra on 3 generators; the first
  deficit appears at length 4 (17 vs 18). This is the analogue of the two-generator case where the first
  non-free identity {V,{V,{V,T}}} = 0 also appears at length 4 (degree 4 in A,B), but here it is a 3-generator,
  inhomogeneous version; no source makes this comparison.

### Gaps
- oeis.org could not be queried (proxy returned CONNECT 403), so the current state/approval of A395423 and any
  cross-references added by editors could not be checked.
- No independent (non-author) appearance of either sequence was found; absence is a search negative, not a
  proof.
